review.notes: Machine-drafted by an AI model; awaiting native-speaker review. Three composite first-person testimonies (a conversion, a healing, a court case), no Scripture quoted; the people are invented. Content note: alcohol, violence in the home, a child with dengue, a false accusation and prison; the Honduran reviewer should confirm they are handled with respect. Variety / register points: evangelical idiom ("nacido de nuevo", "hermanos", "gloria a Dios"), voseo among spouses (no tomés, volvé, tenés), usted for the judge, "cipote", "tomar" for drinking alcohol, "pulpería", "carro prestado", "azote" for the dengue epidemic, "sepulcros" (the planned word; people usually say cementerio), "cuán" (literary; the plan lists it as receptive), "suspenso" (here: waiting without knowing), "juntando" (gathering money). Check that the court scene (a witness testifies against his own father) is plausible in a Honduran court. Vocabulary plan: Pack of PLAN-B1 3.3 for es-b1-21 (testimony: pálido, persiguen..., 53 slots); 12 slots that do not belong in a modern testimony (sinagogo, príncipe, tribuna, romano, puercos, demonio, panoli, potestad, visiones, colocación, aquélla, cabellera) were dropped and logged; persiguen is not used.

english.source: drafted with the text; not reviewed

sentences.text: El primer domingo de cada mes, en la iglesia de la aldea no hay sermón.
sentences.english: On the first Sunday of every month there is no sermon at the village church.

sentences.text: Ese día, el pastor Mario deja hablar a los hermanos que quieran contar algo.
sentences.english: On that day Pastor Mario lets the members who want to tell something speak.

sentences.text: Esta vez se levantaron tres personas: Pedro, Elena y don José.
sentences.english: This time three people stood up: Pedro, Elena and don José.

sentences.text: Los demás escuchaban en silencio, y nadie miraba la hora.
sentences.english: The rest listened in silence, and nobody looked at the time.

sentences.text: Buenas noches, hermanos.
sentences.english: Good evening, brothers and sisters.

sentences.text: Hoy soy un hombre nacido de nuevo, pero no siempre fui así.
sentences.english: Today I am a man born again, but I was not always like this.

sentences.text: Yo nací en Olancho, y desde cipote me gustaba tomar.
sentences.english: I was born in Olancho, and from the time I was a kid I liked drinking.

sentences.text: A los treinta años ya llevaba media vida tomando, y ni yo mismo lo veía.
sentences.english: By the age of thirty I had spent half my life drinking, and I did not even see it myself.

sentences.text: Eso es estar atado, aunque uno nunca lo reconozca.
sentences.english: That is what being tied up is, even if you never admit it.

sentences.text: Yo estaba atado a la botella, y para mí era sólo un capricho.
sentences.english: I was tied to the bottle, and to me it was only a whim.

sentences.text: Hoy sé que aquello no era un capricho, sino una cadena.
sentences.english: Today I know that it was not a whim but a chain.

sentences.text: Mi esposa me decía: «Pedro, no tomés más», y yo contestaba que era un capricho de hombre y que podía dejarlo cuando quisiera.
sentences.english: My wife used to say, "Pedro, don't drink any more," and I would answer that it was a man's whim and that I could quit whenever I wanted.

sentences.text: Una noche, en un arrebato, le grité cosas muy feas delante de nuestros hijos.
sentences.english: One night, in a fit of anger, I shouted very ugly things at her in front of our children.

sentences.text: Aquel arrebato me costó muchas lágrimas, y no fue el único arrebato de esos años.
sentences.english: That fit of anger cost me many tears, and it was not the only one of those years.

sentences.text: Mi hija mayor se escondió en un rincón de la casa, y nunca voy a olvidar su cara.
sentences.english: My oldest daughter hid in a corner of the house, and I will never forget her face.

sentences.text: Salí a la calle y caminé hasta los sepulcros, al otro lado del pueblo.
sentences.english: I went out into the street and walked as far as the graves, on the other side of the town.

sentences.text: Esa noche dormí entre los sepulcros, y sentí un espanto que no puedo explicar.
sentences.english: That night I slept among the graves, and I felt a dread that I cannot explain.

sentences.text: Nadie sabe lo que es el silencio entre los sepulcros cuando uno sabe que ha hecho daño.
sentences.english: Nobody knows what the silence among the graves is like when you know you have done harm.

sentences.text: Tenía espanto de mí mismo, y el espanto no me dejaba dormir.
sentences.english: I was afraid of myself, and the fear would not let me sleep.

sentences.text: Lo que había hecho me atormentaba, y por primera vez me dio lástima de mí mismo y de mi familia.
sentences.english: What I had done tormented me, and for the first time I felt pity for myself and for my family.

sentences.text: Esa lástima fue el principio de todo, porque la lástima me hizo llorar.
sentences.english: That pity was the beginning of everything, because the pity made me cry.

sentences.text: Entonces recordé una cosa que decía el pastor: «Hay un Salvador que no se cansa de buscar a los perdidos».
sentences.english: Then I remembered something the pastor used to say: "There is a Saviour who never tires of looking for the lost."

sentences.text: Yo no creía mucho, pero esa noche me atormentaba tanto la culpa que pedí ayuda a ese Salvador.
sentences.english: I did not believe much, but that night the guilt tormented me so much that I asked that Saviour for help.

sentences.text: También me atormentaba pensar en mis hijos, y por eso no me dormí.
sentences.english: It also tormented me to think about my children, and that is why I did not fall asleep.

sentences.text: Al salir el sol oí en el silencio algo semejante a un susurro.
sentences.english: At sunrise I heard in the silence something like a whisper.

sentences.text: Era un susurro suave, y decía: «Volvé a tu casa».
sentences.english: It was a soft whisper, and it said: "Go back to your house."

sentences.text: Creo que ese susurro fue la voz de Dios.
sentences.english: I believe that whisper was the voice of God.

sentences.text: Volví, y mi esposa estaba en la puerta, con los ojos rojos de llorar.
sentences.english: I went back, and my wife was at the door, her eyes red from crying.

sentences.text: No me gritó ni me castigó con palabras.
sentences.english: She did not shout at me or punish me with words.

sentences.text: Sólo me dijo: «Estoy contigo, pero tenés que cambiar».
sentences.english: She only said to me: "I am with you, but you have to change."

sentences.text: Ese domingo vine a esta iglesia, y mi encuentro con Cristo fue como el resplandor del sol después de una noche larga.
sentences.english: That Sunday I came to this church, and my meeting with Christ was like the radiance of the sun after a long night.

sentences.text: Fue un encuentro de pocos minutos: unas manos, una oración, un resplandor en el corazón.
sentences.english: It was a meeting of a few minutes: some hands, a prayer, a radiance in the heart.

sentences.text: Después de ese encuentro todavía me caí dos veces, porque yo no soy perfecto.
sentences.english: After that meeting I still fell twice, because I am not perfect.

sentences.text: Pero Dios no pide que uno sea perfecto; pide que uno vuelva.
sentences.english: But God does not ask us to be perfect; he asks us to come back.

sentences.text: Ser nacido de nuevo no quiere decir ser perfecto, y hoy no soy perfecto, pero ya no soy un hombre atado.
sentences.english: Being born again does not mean being perfect, and today I am not perfect, but I am no longer a tied-up man.

sentences.text: No quiero ofender a los que no creen, pero esto fue lo que me pasó a mí.
sentences.english: I do not want to offend those who do not believe, but this is what happened to me.

sentences.text: Gracias, hermanos, por no cansarse de mí.
sentences.english: Thank you, brothers and sisters, for not growing tired of me.

sentences.text: Buenas noches.
sentences.english: Good evening.

sentences.text: Voy a hablar de mi hija Rosa, que hoy está sentada allá atrás y se ríe porque se pone roja.
sentences.english: I am going to talk about my daughter Rosa, who is sitting back there today and laughing because she is turning red.

sentences.text: Hace dos años el dengue llegó a nuestra aldea como un azote.
sentences.english: Two years ago dengue came to our village like a scourge.

sentences.text: Ese azote no perdonó a ninguna casa, y yo pensé que a la mía no iba a llegar.
sentences.english: That scourge spared no house, and I thought it would not reach mine.

sentences.text: No entendía por qué ese azote había caído sobre mi hija.
sentences.english: I did not understand why that scourge had fallen on my daughter.

sentences.text: Pero el contagio llegó primero a Rosa, y yo pensé: «Es sólo fiebre, ya va a pasar».
sentences.english: But the infection reached Rosa first, and I thought: "It is only a fever, it will pass."

sentences.text: El contagio fue rápido, y en dos días media familia estaba enferma.
sentences.english: The infection spread fast, and in two days half the family was ill.

sentences.text: Ese contagio se llevó a dos vecinos de nuestra calle.
sentences.english: That infection took two neighbours from our street.

sentences.text: La fiebre no pasó, y mi hija estaba cada día más pálida.
sentences.english: The fever did not pass, and my daughter got paler every day.

sentences.text: Alarmada, y con mi marido lejos, no sabía qué hacer.
sentences.english: Alarmed, and with my husband far away, I did not know what to do.

sentences.text: Alarmada como estaba, llamé a mi mamá, y ella tampoco pudo venir.
sentences.english: Alarmed as I was, I called my mother, and she could not come either.

sentences.text: Se puso pálida como una hoja, y yo me puse pálida también.
sentences.english: She turned pale as a leaf, and I turned pale too.

sentences.text: La clínica estaba cerrada, y el hospital quedaba a tres horas de camino.
sentences.english: The clinic was closed, and the hospital was three hours away by road.

sentences.text: Alarmada, salí a la calle a pedir ayuda.
sentences.english: Alarmed, I went out into the street to ask for help.

sentences.text: No teníamos carro ni dinero, y fui a ver a doña Marta, la dueña de la pulpería.
sentences.english: We had no car and no money, and I went to see doña Marta, the owner of the little shop.

sentences.text: Ella no me hizo ni una pregunta; sólo abrió la caja y me dio lo que tenía.
sentences.english: She did not ask me a single question; she just opened the till and gave me what she had.

sentences.text: La dueña de la pulpería es así: no habla mucho, pero está siempre.
sentences.english: The owner of the little shop is like that: she does not talk much, but she is always there.

sentences.text: Nunca me olvido de lo que hizo esa dueña por mi hija.
sentences.english: I never forget what that owner did for my daughter.

sentences.text: Esa noche, juntando lo poco que teníamos y lo que dieron los vecinos, llevamos a la niña al hospital en un carro prestado.
sentences.english: That night, putting together the little we had and what the neighbours gave, we took the girl to the hospital in a borrowed car.

sentences.text: Las vecinas siguieron juntando comida y ropa para nosotros durante esa semana.
sentences.english: The neighbours went on gathering food and clothes for us during that week.

sentences.text: Los doctores dijeron: «Hay que esperar tres días».
sentences.english: The doctors said: "We have to wait three days."

sentences.text: Y esperar es lo más difícil, porque uno queda en suspenso, sin poder hacer nada.
sentences.english: And waiting is the hardest thing, because you are left in suspense, unable to do anything.

sentences.text: Durante dos noches viví en suspenso, juntando fuerzas para no llorar.
sentences.english: For two nights I lived in suspense, gathering strength so as not to cry.

sentences.text: La tercera noche yo estaba sentada junto a la cama, y no podía orar, porque no encontraba palabras.
sentences.english: On the third night I was sitting beside the bed and I could not pray, because I could not find words.

sentences.text: En esa tercera noche me sentí sola y en suspenso, como si el tiempo se hubiera parado.
sentences.english: On that third night I felt alone and in suspense, as if time had stopped.

sentences.text: Me senté en un rincón del cuarto, para no despertarla.
sentences.english: I sat in a corner of the room, so as not to wake her.

sentences.text: Entonces escuché una voz bajita: era mi hija, que me pedía agua.
sentences.english: Then I heard a little voice: it was my daughter, asking me for water.

sentences.text: Le toqué la frente, y ya no estaba caliente.
sentences.english: I touched her forehead, and it was no longer hot.

sentences.text: Cuando salió el sol, el resplandor de la ventana cayó sobre su cara, y el color había vuelto.
sentences.english: When the sun came up, the radiance from the window fell on her face, and the colour had come back.

sentences.text: No quiero ofender a los doctores, que trabajaron mucho y nos cuidaron bien.
sentences.english: I do not want to offend the doctors, who worked hard and took good care of us.

sentences.text: Tampoco quiero ofender a nadie que no cree, porque yo tampoco creía.
sentences.english: Nor do I want to offend anyone who does not believe, because I did not believe either.

sentences.text: Pero los hermanos de la iglesia habían formado una cadena de oración desde el primer día.
sentences.english: But the brothers and sisters of the church had formed a chain of prayer from the very first day.

sentences.text: Yo no sé cuántas personas tenía esa cadena, pero sé que no se rompió.
sentences.english: I do not know how many people that chain had, but I know it did not break.

sentences.text: Una cadena de oración es una cadena de manos, y cada mano sostiene a la otra.
sentences.english: A chain of prayer is a chain of hands, and each hand holds up the next.

sentences.text: Yo les pregunté a los doctores lo que había acontecido, y ellos sólo dijeron: «Su hija tiene suerte».
sentences.english: I asked the doctors what had happened, and they only said: "Your daughter is lucky."

sentences.text: Yo sé lo que había acontecido en esa habitación, y también sé lo que había acontecido en esta iglesia.
sentences.english: I know what had happened in that room, and I also know what had happened in this church.

sentences.text: Hoy mi hija corre, juega y me hace enojar, y le doy gracias a Dios por cada una de esas cosas.
sentences.english: Today my daughter runs, plays and makes me angry, and I thank God for each one of those things.

sentences.text: Hermanos, ya soy un hombre viejo, pero esto me pasó hace diez años.
sentences.english: Brothers and sisters, I am an old man now, but this happened to me ten years ago.

sentences.text: Yo trabajaba cuidando una tienda, y un día faltó dinero.
sentences.english: I worked looking after a shop, and one day money went missing.

sentences.text: El dueño me acusó de robar, y me llevaron a la prisión.
sentences.english: The owner accused me of stealing, and they took me to prison.

sentences.text: Nunca había oído algo tan feo, y yo no sabía cómo defenderme.
sentences.english: I had never heard anything so ugly, and I did not know how to defend myself.

sentences.text: Yo no tenía abogado ni dinero, y estuve encerrado dos meses antes del juicio.
sentences.english: I had no lawyer and no money, and I was shut up for two months before the trial.

sentences.text: Encerrado en un cuarto pequeño, yo me preguntaba cuánto iba a durar todo.
sentences.english: Shut up in a small room, I wondered how long all this was going to last.

sentences.text: Seguí encerrado hasta el día del juicio, sin saber nada de mi casa.
sentences.english: I stayed shut up until the day of the trial, knowing nothing about my home.

sentences.text: En la cárcel estaba rodeado de hombres con miedo, y yo también tenía temor.
sentences.english: In jail I was surrounded by frightened men, and I was afraid too.

sentences.text: El temor es un mal amigo: no deja comer ni dormir.
sentences.english: Fear is a bad friend: it lets you neither eat nor sleep.

sentences.text: Vivir con temor es peor que vivir sin comida.
sentences.english: Living in fear is worse than living without food.

sentences.text: La prisión es un lugar donde uno piensa, y yo pensaba en mi esposa y en mi casa.
sentences.english: Prison is a place where one thinks, and I thought about my wife and my home.

sentences.text: Mi esposa me contó que esperaba un hijo, y que el nacimiento iba a ser mientras yo estaba en la cárcel.
sentences.english: My wife told me she was expecting a child, and that the birth was going to happen while I was in jail.

sentences.text: Esa fue la parte más dura, porque un varón quiere estar con su familia en el nacimiento de un hijo.
sentences.english: That was the hardest part, because a man wants to be with his family at the birth of a child.

sentences.text: Yo era un varón solo, rodeado de otros varones, y sin saber nada del juicio.
sentences.english: I was a lonely man, surrounded by other men, and knowing nothing about the trial.

sentences.text: Los hombres que me rodeaban eran de todo tipo, y algunos eran buenos.
sentences.english: The men around me were of every kind, and some of them were good.

sentences.text: Pero una noche, en la cárcel, una voz me dijo: «No te voy a dejar solo».
sentences.english: But one night in jail a voice said to me: "I am not going to leave you alone."

sentences.text: Desde entonces sentí una tranquilidad que nadie podía explicar, una tranquilidad que no era mía.
sentences.english: From then on I felt a calm that nobody could explain, a calm that was not mine.

sentences.text: Yo no sabía cuánto iba a durar esa tranquilidad, pero no se fue.
sentences.english: I did not know how long that calm would last, but it did not go away.

sentences.text: El día del juicio, el juez preguntó si había algún testigo a mi favor.
sentences.english: On the day of the trial the judge asked if there was a witness in my favour.

sentences.text: Nadie respondió, y yo pensé que todo estaba perdido.
sentences.english: Nobody answered, and I thought that everything was lost.

sentences.text: Entonces se abrió la puerta, y entró un muchacho que yo conocía de vista: era el hijo del dueño.
sentences.english: Then the door opened, and in came a young man I knew by sight: he was the owner's son.

sentences.text: Venía a testificar contra su propio padre, y ese testigo no tenía miedo.
sentences.english: He had come to testify against his own father, and that witness was not afraid.

sentences.text: Para testificar contra un padre hace falta mucho valor.
sentences.english: It takes a lot of courage to testify against a father.

sentences.text: Dijo que su papá había tomado el dinero, y que me había acusado para esconder la verdad.
sentences.english: He said his father had taken the money, and that he had accused me to hide the truth.

sentences.text: Otros dos testigos hablaron después, y el juez los escuchó con atención.
sentences.english: Two other witnesses spoke afterwards, and the judge listened to them closely.

sentences.text: No sé quién los llamó a testificar, pero llegaron a tiempo.
sentences.english: I do not know who called them to testify, but they arrived in time.

sentences.text: El juez me miró y dijo: «Señor José, usted está libre».
sentences.english: The judge looked at me and said: "Mr José, you are free."

sentences.text: Cuán largos habían sido esos dos meses, y cuán rápido fue ese momento.
sentences.english: How long those two months had been, and how fast that moment was.

sentences.text: Esa tarde salí de la prisión, y cuando llegué a mi casa, mi hijo ya tenía dos meses.
sentences.english: That afternoon I walked out of prison, and when I got home my son was already two months old.

sentences.text: No quiero castigar a nadie, ni siquiera al dueño, porque Dios sabe castigar mejor que yo, y yo también soy un pecador.
sentences.english: I do not want to punish anyone, not even the owner, because God knows how to punish better than I do, and I am a sinner too.

sentences.text: Sólo quiero decirles: si alguna vez los acusan sin razón y se sienten solos, recuerden la voz que oí yo: «Estoy contigo».
sentences.english: I only want to tell you: if you are ever accused without reason and feel alone, remember the voice I heard: "I am with you."

sentences.text: Cuando don José se sentó, el pastor Mario dijo en voz baja: «Cuán grande es lo que acaban de oír».
sentences.english: When don José sat down, Pastor Mario said quietly: "How great is what you have just heard."

sentences.text: Después cantaron todos juntos, y Pedro abrazó a su esposa.
sentences.english: Afterwards they all sang together, and Pedro hugged his wife.
